Clause: In essence the clause prohibits you from hiring any of our key people, either currently in our employment or formerly with us. This could affect both former employees who were involved in the services provision (and who therefore are considered 'trade rivals') as well as currently employed employees. This could also catch you should you decide to solicit any 'unqualified individuals' who may then become 'affiliated agents'. Further the clause could restrict you from doing general recruitment drives where key people, previously employed by us, could 'find their way' into your workforce. It is a fairly un-draughted clause and in many respects a very one-sided document. A far more appropriate alternative could be: a period of time during which non compete and 'sweetner' restraints should operate if such employees join the acquirer (to prevent competing immediately post sale). However this period should only include all 'trade related people', and not all employees with a view to preventing a total ex-sale lock up.

# FERPA clause parsing

This data class is a wrapper dataclass for a json struct that defines 
an FERPA clause to extract or parse using natural language processing.
In order to generate the final struct, this is converted to json (by means 
of json_dot.to_dict()). The resulting dict contains three key objects:
1) the entire json that was used to generate the structure;
2) a nested dict of 'parsed_clauses', which will contain all the clauses
to parse;
3) and an optional 'entities' dict with all the entities found within 
parsed_clauses dictionary structure. This was added because we wanted 
to make sure we also had a record of which terms/clauses we were analyzing
as a team, regardless of whether we identified those terms within this class.
Once we have a record of all the terms/clauses/etc that we're interested
in, we can use that information to pull all relevant terms/clauses 
from other classes of docs (agreements and contracts, for ex., for which we 
want to capture what terms are/not agreed upon) to inform the creation of an 
interesting visual to aid in collaboration amongst team members as well as 
enlarge the breadth of what we can capture around each given piece of data
we're capturing.
